prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1009; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The damage is mostly in line with the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- Records show the same major damage from an earlier, unreported accident; it is now claimed as new.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Reported a left-turn collision at an intersection this morning. The other driver, who is named on our policy, says they were struck while the insured was turning across their path.

Entry 2: Claimant is represented by counsel, who has asked that all contact go through their office. Sent the acknowledgment letter and opened a bodily injury file alongside the property damage file.

Entry 3: Obtained statements from two independent witnesses, both of whom describe the same sequence of events the driver gave. Police report confirms the claimant was in the vehicle at the time of impact.

Entry 4: Photos from the scene and the vehicles are consistent with the impact described. Damage to the front of the claimant's car lines up with the other vehicle's rear quarter panel.

Entry 5: Estimate is in and the bulk of the damage fits the force of a side impact of this type. Appraiser flagged a structural area that appears to have been repaired before, and I have asked for the prior repair records.

Entry 6: Prior claim history shows an earlier accident to the same vehicle, which was never reported to us or to the prior carrier. The same major damage appears in the records from that event and is now being presented as new.

Entry 7: Spoke with the claimant's attorney, who confirmed the client's account of the crash and provided medical notes. The claimant has given the same description in every conversation so far, and there is no sign that the coverage period began after the loss.

Entry 8: Medical records describe neck pain and stiffness consistent with whiplash from this kind of impact. No earlier problems with the same area of the body appear in the records we have.

Entry 9: Treatment followed a typical course, with physical therapy tapering off as the claimant improved. The physician's latest note indicates the claimant is nearly back to normal and expects to be discharged soon.

Entry 10: Reviewing the prior repair records against the current estimate before I make a decision on the property damage. Will confirm the overlap with the earlier accident with the appraiser and the attorney before setting a settlement position on either the vehicle or the injury claim.
